fields.options:
Add this to your Print Format's HTML. The stamp's size comes directly from the anchor text itself - :WxH at the end (in points; roughly px at 96dpi) - so there's no separate Width/Height field to keep in sync with your HTML by hand:

<div style="display:inline-block; position:relative; width:160px; height:80px; margin:4px 0;">
  <span style="color:#ffffff; position:absolute; left:0; bottom:0;">##DIGITAL_SIGN_ANCHOR:160x80##</span>
</div>

Keep the div's own width/height matching the number in the anchor text exactly - the div reserves the layout space so the stamp doesn't overlap surrounding content, and the anchor text tells the signing code how big to actually draw the stamp; if the two disagree, the stamp will be sized correctly but may not fit the space you reserved for it.

160x80 is a reasonable default with every stamp field enabled (signer/reason/location/date/certificate serial - up to 5 lines of text). Leaving off the :WxH suffix entirely (plain ##DIGITAL_SIGN_ANCHOR##) falls back to 160x80 automatically.

The stamp's bottom-left corner is placed exactly where the anchor text sits, so position:absolute; left:0; bottom:0; pins it to the box's own bottom-left corner. The stamp content is centered (both directions) within that box automatically.

Use color:#ffffff (matching the background), not opacity:0 - some PDF engines skip painting opacity:0 text entirely, dropping it from the searchable text layer too. If the surrounding background isn't white, match this color to it instead.
